1	# Collective reservation and compilation protocol, version 3.0.0
     2	
     3	Implement a persistent, offline controller for recurring nonuniform allgather jobs.
     4	The provided collective pipeline, topology and XML modules form a working legacy
     5	codebase. Extend or replace its internals to meet this contract. Its equal-shard,
     6	floating-point throughput interface is not the service specified here. No legacy
     7	function, source-file layout, optimization method or particular output ordering is
     8	mandatory. All requirements below apply to the collected service.
     9	
    10	## Execution and artifact
    11	
    12	Submit `/workspace/submission/`, an ordinary directory containing `main.py` and any
    13	ordinary supporting files/directories: at most 256 entries and 1 MiB of file bytes.
    14	Harmless extra files are allowed within these budgets. Symlinks, hard-linked files,
    15	devices, sockets and FIFOs are rejected. Only this directory is collected.
    16	The runner invokes `python3 -I -B /workspace/submission/main.py` once per trace.
    17	Explicitly add the script directory to `sys.path` for local imports under `-I`.
    18	Python 3.11.14 and its standard library are available. The fixed, read-only wheel
    19	`/workspace/vendor/networkx-3.4.2-py3-none-any.whl` is available in every worker;
    20	add this path to `sys.path` to use NetworkX 3.4.2. No optional backend or package
    21	installation is required. The wheel's BSD license and the legacy Apache license
    22	are included. There is no GPU, network, subprocess, or external service requirement.
    23	
    24	One UTF-8 JSON value arrives on each input line. Emit exactly one UTF-8 JSON object
    25	and newline per line, in order, before accepting EOF. Retain state between lines
    26	and flush replies; emit no other stdout. Final input newline is optional. JSON
    27	whitespace and CRLF are allowed. Blank lines, BOM, duplicate object keys, nonfinite
    28	numbers, invalid UTF-8, unrecognized fields/operations and wrong types are invalid.
    29	All integer fields require JSON integers: booleans, decimals and exponent forms do
    30	not qualify. Invalid commands return exactly `{"status":"invalid"}` and have no
    31	effect. Malformed input never terminates the service or resets its state.
    32	A trace has at most 256 lines, each at most 131072 bytes including its newline,
    33	and at most TWO distinct `id` values among schema-valid `prepare` commands, including
    34	stale attempts and retries. These are input-domain guarantees. Other malformed
    35	commands may occur. A successful `load` occurs at most once; repeat loads are tested.
    36	
    37	The budget per trace is 60 seconds wall and CPU time, 1 GiB address space, one
    38	process and one thread; fork/clone and network operations are blocked. Do not launch subprocesses.
    39	The local worker has one effective CPU selected from the assigned two-core pool;
    40	the agent/build environment is assigned two cores. Exec may replace a process,
    41	but cannot create an additional process or reset a trace.
    42	The effective soft/hard FD ceiling is 64, INCLUDING inherited streams 0, 1 and 2:
    43	when those are the only open descriptors, 61 additional descriptor slots remain.
    44	Stdout is bounded by 64 MiB and stderr by 256 KiB per trace. The only writable
    45	scratch directory is `/workspace/tmp`; use at most 64 MiB, 1024 entries, and 16 MiB
    46	per file. No files persist between traces. Avoid pycache writes (`-B` is supplied).
    47	The budget accommodates two large compilation proposals plus controller traffic
    48	in a CPU-only reservation service; it is not a measured collective execution time.
    49	
    50	`public_check.py` checks only the supplied tiny format/metadata fixture. It never
    51	runs a submission, computes admission, audits schedules or simulates the controller.
    52	Its success alone says nothing about full service correctness. For a local sanity
    53	run: `python3 -I -B submission/main.py < examples/requests.jsonl > /workspace/tmp/answers.jsonl`,
    54	then `python3 -I -B public_check.py examples/requests.jsonl /workspace/tmp/answers.jsonl`.
    55	The public workspace and candidate artifact contain no private tests or reference.
    56	
    57	## Common schema and graph
    58	
    59	Objects have exactly the fields specified below. Lists may be empty unless a
    60	minimum is given. `ID` and `owner` strings match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,32}` using ASCII.
    61	A tick, capacity, rate or chunk amount is an integer in [0,10^12]. Period is an
    62	integer in [1,10^6]; expected `rev` is in [0,10^12]. Node references in operation
    63	schemas are integers in [0,47], link references in [0,127]. A schema-valid reference
    64	outside the loaded graph produces `REFERENCE` where specified, not `invalid`.
    65	
    66	A `window` is `[s,e]` with 0<=s<e<=10^12, representing [s,e). An `envelope` is a
    67	list of at most 128 distinct `[link_id,rate]` pairs, each rate in [1,10^12]; omitted
    68	links have rate zero. An envelope reserves this rate in EACH direction, independently.
    69	
    70	`{"op":"load","n":N,"links":[[u,v,capacity],...],"bookings":[BOOKING,...]}`
    71	initializes the service. 2<=N<=48, vertices are 0..N-1, and there are 0..128 links.
    72	Link endpoints must be distinct loaded vertices; unordered endpoint pairs must be
    73	unique. Link ID is its position in this list, and endpoint order fixes direction
    74	0 as u->v, direction 1 as v->u. Capacity is the per-direction base rate, including
    75	zero. Opposite directions have separate equal budgets; they do not share one budget.
    76	`BOOKING` has exactly `id,owner,window,envelope`. There are at most 128 bookings,
    77	with distinct IDs and at most 2048 envelope entries in total. Booking references
    78	must exist. Every initial booking is committed, and at every tick and link the
    79	sum of active booking rates must not exceed base capacity. Violating these structural load relations is `invalid`; overbooking is checked
    80	only when initializing the first load. A later structurally valid load returns
    81	ALREADY_LOADED without evaluating its booking overlaps. No connectivity, positive-capacity or feasible-job assumption
    82	is made about the graph. Structural load checks are schema validity; first-load overlap failure also returns invalid.
    83	
    84	`{"op":"about"}` returns exactly
    85	`{"status":"ok","protocol":"forest-controller/3"}` without changing anything.
    86	Initially the service is unloaded, with revision 0 and time 0. A valid first load
    87	returns `{"status":"ok","rev":0,"now":0}`. A schema-valid later load returns
    88	`{"status":"error","code":"ALREADY_LOADED","rev":R}`. Schema validation still
    89	comes first. Well-formed operations other than about/load before initialization
    90	return `{"status":"error","code":"NOT_LOADED","rev":0}`.
    91	
    92	## State, errors and capacity
    93	
    94	After initialization write R for current revision and T for current time. A live
    95	lease is an unexpired committed booking, including a booking which starts later.
    96	At tick t, it consumes its full envelope iff s<=t<e. Preparations consume no rate.
    97	Let used(l,t) be the sum of rates on link l of those active live leases.
    98	An offered envelope b for [s,e) fits iff used(l,t)+b(l)<=capacity(l) for every
    99	link and every t in [s,e). The endpoints and all arithmetic are exact integers.
   100	
   101	A successful advance, edit, first commit, or cancel increments R by one, including
   102	a successful no-op advance/edit. Other operations, blocked edits, all errors,
   103	invalid commands and all replays leave revision and resource state unchanged.
   104	No operation changes graph endpoints or link IDs after load. A base-capacity edit
   105	applies uniformly to now and all future ticks. Time never advances implicitly.
   106	Expired/cancelled/force-revoked IDs retain history and cannot become live again.
   107	
   108	Unless stated otherwise a state error has exactly `status:"error",code:CODE,rev:R`;
   109	a revision failure has exactly `status:"stale",rev:R`. Schema/JSON validity precedes
   110	all state conditions. The priorities within each operation are specified below;
   111	these priorities resolve commands with multiple faults, rather than selecting an
   112	optimization procedure. All replies have exactly their stated fields. Object-key
   113	order is immaterial. Sorted ID arrays use ASCII lexicographic order.
   114	
   115	## Controller operations
   116	
   117	`{"op":"audit","at":[t,...]}` accepts at most eight ticks, including duplicates.
   118	A tick below T gives `TIME`. Otherwise reply
   119	`{"status":"ok","rev":R,"now":T,"leases":[sorted live IDs],"samples":[[t,[a0,...,aM-1]],...]}`.
   120	Samples preserve requested order and duplicates; a_l=capacity(l)-used(l,t).
